title: Observation and inference: how scientists know
subject: SCIENCE

objectives.statement: Distinguish observations (what the senses or instruments detect) from inferences (explanations drawn from observations), and suggest an observation that tests an inference.

moe.note: MOE Grade 7 General Science: 'Organize some simple methods of acquiring scientific knowledge'. Observation and inference are proposed as the first such method.

objectives.statement: Record qualitative observations without judgment and quantitative observations as a number with a unit.

moe.note: MOE Grade 7: 'Demonstrate the use of the two systems of measurement in solving problems'. This lesson uses metric units only; the two-systems comparison stays with that MOE lesson.

successCriteria.independentPerformance: Without notes, the learner correctly sorts statements into observations and inferences, names the observations behind an inference, offers a second plausible inference and an observation that would decide between them, and does this in an unrehearsed context such as a clinic record.

Without help, the learner rewrites vague or judgmental records as precise qualitative descriptions and measured quantitative observations with correct units, and still remembers to include units one week later.

prerequisites: Can read a ruler or measuring cylinder to the nearest whole unit and write the unit (e.g. 7 cm).
Can name the five senses and what each one detects.

layers.nationalFoundation: Observation, inference and measured records as the first methods of scientific knowledge in MOE Grade 7 General Science.
layers.liberiaLearnMastery: Rubric-scored reasoning about competing inferences and discriminating observations, misconception-specific feedback, unscaffolded recording and a 7-day retrieval.
layers.globalExcellence: Transfer to a clinic record, which separates measured, reported and inferred information, and an optional measurement-uncertainty challenge.
